label: def:archimedean-realization-functor
title: Archimedean realization functor $\mathcal{R}_{\mathrm{top}}$
html:
Definition. The archimedean realization functor \mathcal{R}_{\mathrm{top}} is the composite

  \mathcal{R}_{\mathrm{top}}
  \;:\;
  \widehat{\mathcal{M}}
  \;\xrightarrow{\;\;\chi_{\mathrm{top}}\;\;}\;
  \widehat{\mathcal{M}} \otimes_{K_0(\mathrm{Var})} \mathbb{Z}
  \;\xrightarrow{\;\;\pi_\infty\;\;}\;
  \mathbb{R}

sending the motivic class [X] to its topological Euler characteristic \chi_{\mathrm{top}}(X) followed by the archimedean projection \pi_\infty \colon \mathbb{A} \to \mathbb{R}. This map evaluates motivic geometric shapes into real-valued physical observables. (The word "functor" in the name and label is legacy: as explained in the follow-on remark, \mathcal{R}_{\mathrm{top}} is a realization / evaluation — a ring homomorphism out of K_0(\mathrm{Var}) — not a functor between categories.)

The action of \chi_{\mathrm{top}} and \pi_\infty, the precise sense in which \mathcal{R}_{\mathrm{top}} is a motivic measure rather than a functor, and its identification with the archimedean component \tau_{\mathrm{arch}} = \pi_\infty \circ \tau of the fibre functor, are developed in the follow-on remark.
